newsitem.title: CANADA: Japan, Peru vow not to yield to "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Japan, Peru vow not to yield to "terrorism".

text.p: Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori vowed at a summit on Saturday not to yield to the demands of guerrillas holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.

Displaying a united front against "terrorism", the two leaders pledged in an official statement, however, to place a premium on the lives of the captives and to seek talks with the rebels without delay.
Hashimoto, who has been uneasy about Peru's tough line with the Tupac Amaru Revloutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, voiced support for Fujimori's handling of the crisis.

"The two leaders strongly condemned the terrorist incident of the seizure of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru as an act unacceptable to either government as well as to the international community and reaffirm their determination not to give in to terrorism," Japan and Peru said in a joint statement in English.

In the communique released after their two-hour meeting at the Sheraton hotel in Toronto, Japan made clear it supported Fujimori's flat refusal to accede to a demand by the MRTA for the release of hundreds of their comrades in Peruvian jails.

"Prime Minister Hashimoto reaffirmed his full confidence in the Peruvian government's handling of this incident and asserted that his government would continue to give its full support to the effort to achieve the shared objective of the release of all the hostages," the communique added.
